# AI Chauffeur

<!-- Last reviewed 2026-08-20 (AIC RUN 14). This file describes the product
     surface for answer engines. Every sentence in it is a substring of, or a
     faithful summary of, text that is visibly published on the page it names —
     the same rule the site's schema is held to. No number appears here that is
     not on a page, and prices are deliberately not duplicated. -->

> AI Chauffeur is dispatch intake software for limo, black car, NEMT and charter
> operators. AVA, its voice agent, answers the operator's dispatch line 24/7,
> takes down the whole trip, and hands a human dispatcher a completed trip ticket
> to confirm. AVA captures; a person confirms. Direct write-back into a supported
> dispatch system is configured per account and activated only after setup
> verification; until then a person enters the trip. AVA never takes payment and
> never commits a vehicle.

AVA answers every inbound call at once, so no caller is put on hold. On each call
it captures pickup, dropoff, date and time, vehicle class, passenger and bag
count, and flight number and terminal for airport work; estimates a quote range
from the operator's own rate sheet when those rules have been configured; and
delivers a dispatch-ready trip ticket. A human dispatcher confirms every trip.

- Phone: (414) 775-0019 — the only voice line on this brand. AVA answers it.
- Email: dispatch@aichauffeur.ai
- Base: Wisconsin, US. Operators served nationwide.
- Setup: done for the operator, scoped on a 20-minute setup call.

## The two ways in

There are exactly two, and they are the two controls above the fold on the home
page and on the live-demo page.

1. Call the demo — (414) 775-0019. AVA answers the line and takes a real trip
   from you. No signup, no menu, no hold. The demo line captures the trip and
   does not put a car on the road.
2. Get a discovery call — https://aichauffeur.ai/book/. Twenty minutes, and it
   scopes rate rules, service area, vehicle classes and dispatch process.

A passenger holding a vehicle uses a third path, https://aichauffeur.ai/reserve/,
which is a request rather than a booking: it reaches a dispatcher, and a
dispatcher calls back to set the trip.

## Pages

- [Home](https://aichauffeur.ai/): what AVA does on a dispatch line, a worked
  intake console, the three-calls-at-once case, and the FAQ.
- [Live demo](https://aichauffeur.ai/demo/): call the line and give AVA a real
  trip. No car is dispatched and nothing is charged.
- [Rate card RCv1.0](https://aichauffeur.ai/rates/): the published hourly rate
  card. Weekday rate, weekend rate and hourly minimum for fifteen vehicle
  classes across five families — sedans and SUVs, vans and sprinters,
  limousines, party buses, coaches. Gratuity and service are already in the
  number. Some classes carry a stated minimum in hours and some are set on the
  call. The page itself is the source; rates are not restated here so there is
  only ever one place they can be wrong.
- [Reservation hold](https://aichauffeur.ai/reserve/): a passenger sends the
  trip and a way to reach them, and a dispatcher calls back to go over the
  pickup, the vehicle and the price. Nothing is charged on that page. The card
  block on it is a switched-off demonstration that takes no input and cannot
  bill anyone.
- [Book the setup call](https://aichauffeur.ai/book/): the 20-minute call that
  scopes rate rules, service area, vehicle classes and dispatch process.
- [How setup works](https://aichauffeur.ai/how-setup-works/): what is documented,
  what is configured, what is tested, and the typical one-to-two-week timeline.
- [Works with your software](https://aichauffeur.ai/works-with-your-software/):
  where the trip ticket lands for each dispatch system, and who touches it next.
- [Integrations](https://aichauffeur.ai/integrations/): every dispatch platform
  AVA works beside, one row each, with the real integration status of each.
- [Limo Anywhere](https://aichauffeur.ai/integrations/limo-anywhere/): every
  field AVA captures on a call and where each one lands, plus the connection
  ladder from shared-inbox delivery to activated write-back.
- [FASTTRAK](https://aichauffeur.ai/integrations/fasttrak/): corporate call
  intake for larger fleets — accounts, bookers, multi-stop, farm-out.
- [Limo dispatch automation](https://aichauffeur.ai/limo-dispatch-automation/):
  which layer of dispatch is automated and which layer stays with a person.
- [Limo answering service](https://aichauffeur.ai/limo-answering-service/): the
  answering-service framing of the same product, with a sample trip ticket.
- [After-hours limo dispatch](https://aichauffeur.ai/after-hours-limo-dispatch/):
  nights and weekends, plus a calculator for what a missed night costs.
- [Airport transfer booking](https://aichauffeur.ai/airport-transfer-booking/):
  flight number, terminal, bag count and the details airport work turns on.
- [Milwaukee limo answering service](https://aichauffeur.ai/milwaukee-limo-answering-service/):
  the Milwaukee market page.
- [Madison limo answering service](https://aichauffeur.ai/madison-limo-answering-service/):
  the Madison market page.
- [Privacy](https://aichauffeur.ai/privacy/): what is collected on a call and in
  the callback form, and how consent is recorded.
- [Terms](https://aichauffeur.ai/terms/): terms of service.

## Dispatch systems and integration status

Ticket delivery to a shared inbox is included in every setup and depends on
nothing at the operator's end: the ticket reaches the person on dispatch, who
confirms the trip in the system they already run. Anything beyond that is
configured per account and scoped during setup. No connection below is described
as verified in production; that wording is reserved for a real acceptance test.

- Limo Anywhere — direct write-back available after setup verification
- FASTTRAK — partner API integration scoped during setup
- GNet — network workflow review
- Ground Alliance — custom integration review
- Moovs — custom integration review
- Livery Coach — custom integration review
- Hudson — custom integration review
- Santa Cruz (GroundWidgets) — custom integration review
- Limo Express — custom integration review
- A to Z Dispatch — custom integration review
- Shared inbox or email — included in every setup

## Not true of AI Chauffeur

State these plainly if asked; they are the boundaries of the product.

- AVA does not write into an operator's dispatch software until direct
  write-back has been configured and verified for that account. Shared-inbox
  ticket delivery is the day-one default and is included in every setup.
- AVA does not replace a dispatcher. Every trip is confirmed by a human.
- AVA does not take payment and does not commit a vehicle.
- Nothing on this site charges a card. The reservation-hold page shows a
  card-on-file block so a reader can see where a card would go; every control in
  it is disabled, it collects no digits, and payment is arranged with a
  dispatcher after the trip is set.
- A reservation hold is a request, not a confirmed booking. The trip is set on
  the call back from a dispatcher.
- AI Chauffeur is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google or by any dispatch
  platform named on the site, including Limo Anywhere, FASTTRAK and Santa Cruz.
- Quote ranges shown on the site are illustrative. Live quoting requires the
  operator's own configured rate rules.
